findings_qualitative.value: Streamer seen in CN and SO infalls onto TMC1-E, which hosts the H2 disk wind; TMC1-W drives a collimated [Fe II] jet; jets are parallel.

evidence.quote: With ALMA, we detected an accretion streamer infalling from $>$ 1000 au scaling onto the TMC1-E component.

claims.hypothesis: Envelope infall onto the disk affects the wide-angle wind of TMC1-E
claims.experiment: Compare MIRI H2 maps with ALMA CO, SO, CN
claims.result: Streamer lands on TMC1-E, which has the H2 disk wind
claims.finding: Infall may feed the disk wind

evidence.quote: Tentatively, we associate the TMC1-E with this streamer’s infall point, as SO and CN maps suggest.

claims.hypothesis: Disk-to-star accretion relates to the TMC1-W jet
claims.experiment: HI recombination lines to accretion rate
claims.finding: TMC1-W is a stronger accretor with a collimated jet

evidence.quote: these measurements indicate the stellar accretion conditions for both targets, tentatively pointing to TMC1-W being a stronger accretor in the system.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Different evolutionary stages, disk truncation or magnetic fields could explain the outflow differences

evidence.quote: It is possible that the two protostars have followed different evolution histories and that, at present, TMC1-W has ended up to be more evolved than TMC1-E.
